novelty_flags.label: AhnKasahara2026 comparisons in comparator_promise_table, related_work, seed S1, and thm:regular-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: The core attributes the regular parameter and ATT results to “Proposition P-2” and “Proposition P-1,” but the cited arXiv version has Proposition 4 for parameter identification and Proposition 5 plus Corollary 1 for LTATT and aggregate ATT identification.

soundness_flags.label: symbols.Z
soundness_flags.one_line: Z is declared to have space \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) but is defined as taking values \(\{1,2\}\), conflicting with every subsequent \(z\in\{1,2\}\) index.

soundness_flags.label: symbols.R and def:terminal-chart-atlas
soundness_flags.one_line: R is defined as a latent conditional probability using P even though P was declared as the observed law; define it as a representation-dependent coordinate (for example \(R(\psi)\)) before using it in the chart equations.

soundness_flags.label: symbols.P_star and thm:benchmark-merger
soundness_flags.one_line: The benchmark description does not specify a full observed PMF, including \(P(D=1)\) and all conditional rows, so \(P^\star\), its membership in \(\mathcal M_\eta\), and the displayed sharp endpoints are not uniquely defined.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 16–17, Proposition 4; p. 17, Proposition 5 and Corollary 1; pp. 28–29, equations (31)–(32) and distinct-eigenvalue recovery step
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 4 uniquely identifies the parameter vector under RSM, M, and ID; Proposition 5 identifies type-specific ATT and Corollary 1 identifies aggregate ATT. The proof uses nonsingular matrices and distinct eigenvalues under Assumption ID.

source_verification_receipts.version: author-hosted January 19, 2023 working-paper version; cited Journal of Econometrics primary version was not inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under Assumptions 1–3, distributions of the initial condition, transition kernels, and type probabilities are identified up to a common latent-type permutation from four consecutive observations.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–10, Section 5, especially Figure 4 discussion and equations defining sharp polynomial-program bounds
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs and uses branch-and-bound dual envelopes to refine bounds, with epsilon-sharpness rather than the proposed specialized exact algebraic component enumeration.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct every Ahn--Kasahara anchor to Proposition 4, Proposition 5, and Corollary 1, and state their exact RSM/M/TI-LT/ID assumptions beside the regular-reduction comparison.

Define \(P^\star\) as a complete rational 32-cell PMF (or a complete rational \(\psi^\star\)), including treatment share and every transition row, then make the endpoint witnesses reproducible from that object.
Replace latent-law notation \(R=P(Z=z,\ldots\mid D=d)\) by explicitly representation-indexed chart coordinates and state the terminal-splitting equations in that coordinate system.

Before advancing, execute the stated one-collided-control-row kill test by displaying the actual finite sign list and both relative-alignment cases for that chart; this would turn the present field-level novelty claim into a credible constructive kernel.

recommended_next_step: Revise the notation and fully specify the benchmark, correct the Ahn--Kasahara comparison anchors, then continue to Stage 0 only after the one-collided-control-chart sign-atlas kill test is made explicit.
